newsitem.title: LEBANON: SOLIDERE no comment on $100 mln GDR issue rumours.
newsitem.headline: SOLIDERE no comment on $100 mln GDR issue rumours.

text.p: Lebanon's biggest company SOLIDERE declined to comment on Friday on market rumours in Beirut that it is preparing to offer Global Depositary Receipts (GDRs) on the international market worth up to $100 million.
Asked about the rumours, a spokesman for the $2 billion real estate company which is rebuilding the war-damaged Beirut city centre told Reuters he had no comment.
A GDR issue on the international market would open up investment in SOLIDERE to foreign investors through a synthetic product linked to the shares, a market source said.

The shares have been publicly traded in Beirut since mid-1994 but are only available to Lebanese and Arab investors. They cannot be bought by other foreigners due to Lebanon's ban on non-Arab ownership of real estate.
Some Beirut market sources said the issue target was $150 million. Others said this had been reduced to $100 million.
SOLIDERE's $100 A and B shares soared to $170 shortly after issue in 1994 but later fell.
They dropped this year to all-time lows of $103 and $105 respectively but picked up recently. On Friday they rose to $108.5 and $111.375 from Thursday's $106.875 and $108.5.
The shares, which have so far been traded on the privately-operated Beirut Secondary Market (BSM), are due to move to the official Beirut Stock Exchange (BSE) on September 30.
